name: Bio-stimulator
summary: Injectable treatments used to support the skin's own structural renewal.
leadAnswer: Bio-stimulators, such as Sculptra, Radiesse and Ellansé, are injectables intended to prompt the skin's own collagen rather than add volume on the day, as a dermal filler does. Any change is gradual, and unlike a hyaluronic acid filler they cannot be dissolved, so a doctor plans the course across months after assessment.
seoDescription: Bio-stimulator injectables in Malaysia, including Sculptra and Ellanse, to support the skin's structural renewal. Book a free consultation at Kaiteki.
typicalSessions: A short course, spaced several weeks apart

facts.label: Supports your own collagen rather than adding volume on the day
Your first visit is a doctor consultation, not a treatment

routes.title: Gradual collagen rebuilding over months
routes.body: Change is deliberately slow, which some people prefer and others find frustrating.

variantModule.heading: Sculptra, Radiesse or Ellansé: which material, and why
variantModule.intro: Each product uses a different base material, which changes how it behaves and how long it takes to resorb.

items.title: Sculptra
items.body: Reconstituted before use and intended to act as a gradual collagen stimulus over a course of sessions. The reconstituting fluid is absorbed within days, so early appearance is not the treatment effect.

items.title: Radiesse
items.body: Support from the gel carrier when it is placed, then a collagen and elastin response as the microspheres are resorbed, with manufacturer-cleared use on the hands and décolletage as well as the face.

items.title: Ellansé
items.body: Support from the carrier gel when it is placed, plus a collagen response as the PCL microspheres are resorbed, supplied in variants that differ in how long the microspheres take to clear.

items.title: Deusaderm
items.body: A collagen-based injectable intended to support skin quality, structure and elasticity.

ctaMid.heading: Not sure whether you need a filler or a bio-stimulator?
ctaMid.body: A doctor can tell you which your concern calls for, or whether it needs neither.

avoidIf.lead: A history of keloid or hypertrophic scarring.

sessionSteps.title: Consultation and assessment
sessionSteps.body: The doctor assesses your skin, confirms suitability, discusses the realistic time course and selects the product.

sessionSteps.title: Preparation
sessionSteps.body: The skin is cleansed and prepared, and topical or local anaesthetic is used for comfort.

sessionSteps.title: The injections
sessionSteps.body: The doctor injects the assessed areas.

sessionSteps.title: Afterwards
sessionSteps.body: The doctor may massage the treated area and explains aftercare, including any massage to do at home.

bands.title: At the injection sites
bands.body: Mild swelling, redness or tenderness may occur and usually settles within a few days. Bruising can occasionally take longer to fade.

bands.title: The first days
bands.body: Avoid pressure or vigorous facial treatments on the area for a short period, and follow any massage instructions given.

afterSession.aftercare: Follow the massage and aftercare instructions you are given for your product.

risks.common: Temporary redness, swelling, bruising or tenderness at the injection sites.
risks.lessCommon: Delayed-onset lumps or nodules have been reported with collagen-stimulating products, sometimes months after treatment, and rare but serious vascular complications are recognised for facial injectables in general.
cannotDo: It does not add volume on the day: change develops gradually over months.
It cannot be dissolved the way a hyaluronic acid filler can.
It is not permanent. The material is resorbed, and your own tissue continues to age.
risks.disclose: Raise any delayed lump, swelling or skin change with the clinic straight away, even months after treatment.

costFactors.intro: Kaiteki does not quote prices online, because the product and the plan are decided at consultation. What moves it:
factors: Which product the doctor selects for your assessment.
The area being addressed, and how much structural support has been lost.
The number of sessions in the course.
Whether periodic maintenance is part of the plan.

relatedReasons.skin-booster: Injectable hydrating treatments for skin quality, where the concern is hydration rather than structure.

sections.heading: What is a bio-stimulator?
body: A bio-stimulator is a type of injectable treatment given by a doctor that is intended to support the skin's own collagen framework, rather than to add immediate volume the way a conventional dermal filler does.

sections.heading: How does a bio-stimulator work with your own collagen?
body: Bio-stimulators are delivered by injection into targeted layers of the skin. The formulation acts as a scaffold within the tissue, and the body is intended to respond by gradually renewing its own supporting structures around it.
Because the response builds gradually and varies between people, review appointments are how change is judged.

faqs.q: Is a bio-stimulator the same as a dermal filler?
faqs.a: No. A dermal filler adds volume directly and, if hyaluronic acid, can be dissolved. A bio-stimulator prompts your own collagen gradually and cannot be dissolved.

faqs.q: Are bio-stimulator treatments suitable for sensitive skin?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but it cannot be assumed. Active inflammation, keloid scarring and autoimmune conditions are the factors the doctor checks first.
Usually minimal: mild swelling, redness or tenderness at the injection sites that settles within a few days. Bruising can take longer.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: Usually a short course spaced several weeks apart, sometimes with periodic maintenance afterwards.
